title: Driven to Diesel?
summary: In a recent interview with the Wall Street Journal, President Bush reiterated his position on decreasing the United States' reliance on foreign oil and changing driving habits to curb gasoline consumption. Homegrown ethanol technology was offered as a solution. He remarked, "It's interesting, this [energy] diversification has required federal involvement-federal involvement through tax credits for ethanol, as well as research dollars." In a market economy, price should be the ultimate determinant of widespread interest in an alternative fuel source in the United States.

children.title: Changing the Mix
children.summary: The largest hurdle for the adoption of diesel or other alternatives in the United States is the secure and ample supply of these alternative products. Refineries in the US are currently geared to maximize production of gasoline at the expense of heavier products.
